record.context_brief: Newton inequalities for stable GKK τ-matrices
record.original_question: Suppose A is a stable GKK τ-matrix. Must A satisfy Newton's inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1}c_{j+1} for every j = 1, ..., n - 1, where c_j denotes the average of the principal minors of order j?

evidence.quote: This problem has possible subproblems, e.g., 5b. Newton’s inequalities for stable GKK τ -matrices.
Does any GKK τ -matrix A satisfy the inequalities c2j ≥ cj−1cj+1, j = 1, . . . , n − 1? (4)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ complex matrix. For each $j=1,\dots,n$, let $c_j(A)$ denote the normalized $j$-th coefficient of the characteristic polynomial, i.e., the average of all principal minors of $A$ of order $j$:
$$c_j(A) = \binom{n}{j}^{-1} \sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}\\|S|=j}} \det(A[S,S]).$$
Set $c_0(A)=1$.

A real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ is called a GKK matrix if every principal minor of $A$ is positive and $A$ is weakly sign-symmetric, meaning that for every pair of indices $i,j$ and every principal submatrix containing rows/columns indexed by $\{i,j\}$, the corresponding "almost principal" minors $\det(A[S\cup\{i\},S\cup\{j\}])$ and $\det(A[S\cup\{j\},S\cup\{i\}])$ have the same sign (or one is zero). A matrix $A$ is a $\tau$-matrix if every principal submatrix $A[S,S]$ satisfies the eigenvalue–monotonicity property: the spectral radius of every principal submatrix of $A[S,S]$ is dominated by the spectral radius of $A[S,S]$ itself. A matrix $A$ is called stable (positively stable) if every eigenvalue of $A$ has positive real part.

Question: Suppose $A$ is a stable GKK $\tau$-matrix. Must $A$ satisfy Newton's inequalities
$$c_j(A)^2 \;\geq\; c_{j-1}(A)\, c_{j+1}(A) \qquad \text{for every } j=1,\dots,n-1?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent result (Holtz, "Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable", 2005) disproved the broader stability conjectures by exhibiting GKK τ-matrices that are not nonnegative stable. However, no source located confirms whether the specific Newton inequality question restricted to stable GKK τ-matrices has been resolved; thus its current status appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: A class of GKK τ-matrices is constructed which are not even nonnegative stable, disproving stability conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability conjectures for GKK τ-matrices were disproved, but the Newton-inequality subproblem for the stable subclass is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Weakly sign-symmetric matrices and some determinantal inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Studies determinantal inequalities for weakly sign-symmetric matrices.
status_evidence.claim: General determinantal inequalities for related matrix classes have been studied but do not appear to settle the Newton inequalities for stable GKK τ-matrices.
